cards.a: Build proteins using instructions from the nucleus, written in mRNA.

cards.q: Why does a pancreas cell have millions of ribosomes?
cards.a: It makes lots of protein - digestive enzymes.

cards.q: Besides ribosomes, what is prominent in protein-making cells?
cards.a: A large nucleolus, where ribosomal subunits are assembled.
Attached to the outside of the ER or the nuclear envelope.

cards.q: Are free and bound ribosomes different structures?
cards.a: No. They are identical and can work in either place, depending on the protein made.

cards.q: What do proteins made by free ribosomes usually do?
cards.a: Work in the cytosol, e.g. enzymes for the first steps of sugar breakdown.

cards.q: What proteins do bound ribosomes typically make?
cards.a: Proteins that will be exported from the cell.

cards.q: What does a ribosome translate mRNA into?
cards.a: The mRNA nucleotide sequence becomes the amino acid sequence of a polypeptide.
